parsedVerdict.reasoning: AssignTaskUseCase.execute does what an application-layer use case is meant to do. It loads aggregates through injected domain repository interfaces and checks that the task and user exist. It hands the business state change to the domain entity through task.assign(userId), saves the result through the repository abstraction, and maps the entity to a TaskDTO. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, ORM or storage calls) and no transport or framework logic (no HTTP, request or response handling). It also holds no business invariants of its own: assignment rules stay in the domain entity. The existence checks that throw "not found" errors are orchestration, which is normal in a use case. Building the DTO, including formatting the date as ISO text, is the boundary mapping the application layer is responsible for.
